title: The page fills its column, and a browser proves it
summary: The watch page's main column is sized by what it holds instead of by the page it sits on, so at 1440 it under-fills by 191px, re-flows the whole page when one card opens, and below the single-column step it spills past its own gutters and gains a sideways scrollbar. This binder fixes that and the five smaller layout gaps the last comparison recorded, and it builds the thing the repo has been missing all along: a way to measure the rendered page in a real browser, so a geometry claim is proven rather than read off the stylesheet.
motivation:
A person opened the pinned-fixture page and called it completely broken. Every check the page has says it is fine, and both statements are true: the page's 258-check self-test reads DECLARED stylesheet values, and the defect is not in any declaration. `body{display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center}` (serve_status.py:1449-1456) is a legal declaration. An app root with no width (`
` at serve_status.py:4337, mounted at :4179) is a legal absence. Together, in a COLUMN flexbox where `align-items` governs the horizontal axis, they size the root shrink-to-fit — so `.wrap{width:100%;max-width:1040px}` (:1481) and `.wrap--repo{max-width:1440px}` (:1485) resolve against a content-sized parent and the cap never binds. A declaration check cannot catch an emergent-layout defect. That is the gap this binder closes, and closing it is why the harness lands first and everything else depends on it. Eight findings own an item each, and the mapping is written down so a gap shows as an absence rather than turning up at a gate. The six the 2026-08-22 run recorded as open: finding 1, the content-sized column, is `column-fills-its-page`; finding 2, the binder card's square progress track, is `binder-track-pill`; findings 3 and 4, the bold eyebrow and the untracked next-action sentence, are both `head-type-weight-and-tracking` — two single declarations in the same head region, honest to take together; finding 5, the tighter spacing scale, is `main-column-spacing-scale`; finding 6, the small type at the card's foot and in its detail, is `card-foot-and-detail-type`. Two more the run could not see, because it was taken at 1440 only and named `any width other than 1440` as unshown: the sideways scrollbar below the single-column step, and the header's repo name spilling instead of truncating, are both `narrow-widths-do-not-spill`. Two items answer to no finding: `geometry-harness` is the measurement the rest depend on, and `measured-fidelity-gate` records the run. Both are named in scope.included rather than inherited from the run. One consequence to state up front, because it is the point rather than a side effect: with real measurement the waiver count should fall. The previous binder parked seven `visual_check_waiver`s because nothing in it could observe a painted result. This one carries two, and both are judgements about how a whole reads rather than claims a measurement could settle. An item here whose claim the harness can measure and that waives anyway would be exactly the regression this binder exists to end. How this binder is gated, stated once because it is the whole point. Every item's oracle is type unit, dispositioned by karta-verify against the diff — the visual gate is not used, because karta-validate's serve_design.py hard-roots at the design file's parent and 404s this repo's eight woff2 faces and its mascot, which is why the previous binder's closing item was unit-typed too. What is different here is the command seven of the eight oracles run: measure_page.py --check (geometry-harness, the instrument itself, runs --self-test instead — pointing --check at the item that builds it would make it ungateable on a browserless machine, where the harness exits 3 and the && chain fails), which opens the served page in a real browser and compares measured geometry against the values that item pins, before the floor runs at all. The page's 258 existing checks all read declared stylesheet values, and the defect this binder starts from — a column flexbox whose align-items sizes the app to its content — is a legal declaration in every one of them. A declaration check cannot see an emergent layout defect. That is the gap, and closing it is item one.

work_items.title: Measure the rendered page in a real browser
work_items.summary: Add a script that boots the page against the pinned fixture, drives playwright-cli to read computed styles and box rectangles at named viewports and named states, and prints one JSON artifact — so every later item can prove a geometry claim by measuring it instead of by reading the stylesheet.

component_map.design: no design counterpart — this is the instrument, not a surface. What it exists to observe is the design's own geometry, read from docs/designs/karta-watch-1440x900-light.html
component_map.implementation: NEW file skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py. It starts serve_status.py the way the runbook does (docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md:17-25), waits for the page to answer, then shells out to playwright-cli (open / goto / resize / click / eval) and reads getComputedStyle and getBoundingClientRect off the live DOM

component_map.design: the runbook already names the two clicks as protocol: click the binder header to open the panel, then expand one card's disclosure (docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md:33-38)
component_map.implementation: the harness names those as its three states rather than leaving them to a caller's improvisation. The fixture binder derives as next and the page opens only the current binder's panel at rest (serve_status.py:3671), so the work-item cards are absent from the DOM until the first click — a probe against a card taken at rest reads nothing, and must report an unreached state rather than an empty value

component_map.design: not applicable
component_map.implementation: the floor picks the script up with no validator edit: _check_skill_scripts sweeps every skills/*/scripts/*.py and runs its --self-test (scripts/validate_plugin.py:1348-1354), and _run_self_test fails distinctly on a script that does not expose --self-test at all (validate_plugin.py:1297-1330). So the pure self-test is in the floor from the moment the file lands, and nothing wires it there by hand

contract.exposes: one stdlib-only script in the house pattern (inline PEP 723 metadata, argparse, a --self-test mode printing [PASS]/[FAIL] lines) that measures the rendered page and prints one JSON artifact on stdout. Named viewports, three named states (at rest, after the binder-panel click, after one card's disclosure click), and a probe grammar of selector plus the computed properties and rect fields to read. Plus a section in the fidelity runbook naming the script by path, the command, the three state names and the skip line. And the mode every other item in this binder gates on: --check <group>, which takes the measurements, compares them against a named group of expected values carried inside the script itself, prints one line per comparison, and exits 0 when they all hold and 1 when any does not. The groups are not written here — each later item adds its own, named for that item, in the same commit as the fix it proves, so the expectation and the change arrive together and karta-verify sees both in one diff. --port defaults to 0, meaning an OS-assigned free port, so a run can never collide with the wave env on 8700 or the multi-repo hub's derived port. And --check all, which runs every named group in one invocation and exits 1 if any group fails or names nothing — the mode the closing gate uses to re-prove every earlier group on the assembled tip.
contract.consumes: serve_status.py as a subprocess, playwright-cli as a subprocess, and the committed fixture. It imports neither and edits nothing.
contract.regression_risk: the sharp edge here is a check that goes green when it could not run. If the browser is missing and the harness exits 0 with an empty artifact, every later item's oracle passes while proving nothing — which is worse than the declaration-only floor this binder is replacing, because it would look like measurement. So the skip path is the one behaviour with its own assertion, its own exit code and its own negative case. The mirror-image risk is a harness whose self-test needs a browser: that would drag the whole floor into needing one, and `uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test` would stop being runnable on a plain machine. Both directions are asserted, in opposite senses.
contract.preserves: the floor stays browser-free. python stays the only runtime scripts/ and skills/*/scripts/ need for `--self-test`; node and playwright-cli are needed only by a measurement run, which the floor never makes. The runtime_contract declares node because every OTHER item's oracle runs a measurement, and karta-build's halt on a missing runtime is the honest outcome for those items — not for the floor.

oracle.command: uv run skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --self-test && env PATH="$(dirname "$(command -v uv)"):/usr/bin:/bin" uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test && uv run --script skills/karta-status/scripts/serve_status.py --self-test && uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test
assertions: the harness boots serve_status.py on the caller's --port rooted at the caller's --root, waits for the page to answer, drives playwright-cli to set each named viewport and reach each named state, and prints ONE JSON artifact on stdout carrying every probe's getComputedStyle values and getBoundingClientRect box — one artifact for the whole run, not one per probe, so a later item quotes a single document

the three states are the two clicks the runbook already calls protocol, named the same way in the artifact: at rest, after the binder-panel click, after one work-item card's disclosure click. A state the run could not reach is reported as unreached with the reason, never as an empty reading — the fixture binder derives as next and the cards are absent from the DOM until the first click (serve_status.py:3671), so an unreached state is a normal outcome and has to be legible as one

when playwright-cli is not on PATH the harness prints the line `SKIPPED — no browser: playwright-cli is not on PATH, so no rendered geometry was measured and nothing below is proven` byte-for-byte, names every viewport and state it did not take, and exits 3 — a code distinct from both 0 (measured) and 1 (ran and something failed). It never prints a measurement it did not take, and it never exits 0 on that path

--check <group> is the gate the rest of this binder hangs on: it runs the measurement, compares each reading against that group's expected value, prints one line per comparison naming the selector, the property, the expected and the measured value, and exits 1 on any mismatch — never 0 with a printed complaint. An unknown group name exits 1 rather than passing vacuously, and a group whose expectations are empty exits 1 for the same reason. The no-browser skip of the assertion above outranks it: without playwright-cli the run exits 3 and no comparison is claimed either way

--self-test runs with no browser and no network: it covers the artifact assembly, the probe grammar, the skip path and the three exit codes over embedded fixtures, prints [PASS]/[FAIL] lines, and exits 0 on a machine with no playwright-cli and no browser installed. The same is proven for the whole floor by running `uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test` with playwright-cli removed from PATH, which must stay green. That claim is proven the only way it can be: the floor is re-run once with playwright-cli removed from PATH — uv and python still resolvable, the browser not — and it passes. Running it on the ordinary host PATH proves nothing about a browserless machine, because the browser is there

every rule the self-test asserts ships with a companion case that fails it (house.4): a probe naming a selector the page does not have fails; a malformed probe spec fails; a run whose server never answers fails with a named reason instead of an empty artifact; and the skip path is exercised against a fixture PATH that has no playwright-cli on it

the harness writes nothing into the repo. It prints to stdout; its only side effects are the server subprocess it starts and the playwright-cli session it opens, and it stops both. A run that leaves either alive fails its own teardown check, which is asserted rather than assumed

the script is stdlib-only with inline PEP 723 metadata, argparse and --self-test, matching the house pattern, and it reaches serve_status.py and playwright-cli through subprocess rather than importing either — the page's own module must stay importable-free of a browser dependency

the fidelity runbook gains a section naming skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py by path, the command that runs it, the three state names and the skip line, so a reader with no browser learns from the runbook what a skipped run does not prove rather than only from the script's output
the regenerated Codex mirrors of measure_page.py under .agents/skills/karta-status/scripts/ and plugins/karta/skills/karta-status/scripts/ are byte-identical to the canonical file

signals: not-computed:sensitive — this repo configures no sensitive-path convention, so that signal could not be evaluated

capability or resource escalation — a new script that starts a server subprocess and drives a browser. Nothing else in this repo does either, and it is picked up by the floor automatically because _check_skill_scripts sweeps skills/*/scripts/*.py (validate_plugin.py:1348-1354), so the pure-self-test rule is not optional

contract mutation — the runtime_contract gains node, so karta-build's preflight halts on a machine without it. That is the intended outcome for the seven items whose oracles measure, and it is written down here rather than left to be met at a halt. Needed by the seven items whose oracles drive playwright-cli, NOT by geometry-harness, whose own oracle is python-only (measure_page.py --self-test plus the floor). Because runtime_contract is binder-wide, on_unavailable: halt stops the whole binder on a node-less machine including that one item — a real over-reach, accepted deliberately: seven of eight items cannot be gated there, so a run that built only the instrument and halted would be a worse outcome than halting at preflight with the reason named. The version floor is playwright-cli's own engines field as installed on the planning host (0.1.15), not a repo pin; a different playwright-cli may want a different node, and an item that hits that states it rather than widening this silently

explicit — this is the architectural half of the binder and the one item most reasonably cut into its own. Everything else depends on it, so if it is cut, the rest of the binder has to fall back to declaration checks and the defect class stays invisible
scope of impact — this item and measured-fidelity-gate both edit docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md, so both declare it as a shared resource and the wave scheduler keeps them apart

contract.exposes: a content column sized by the page: the same width at rest and with the panel open, at the design's 1376 measure at a 1440 viewport, with the gutter stated once as a named constant that the body rule and the header's bleed both read.
contract.consumes: the harness from geometry-harness — every width claim here is measured with measure_page.py, not read off the sheet.
contract.regression_risk: this is the change the run's own text warns about: a change here moves every width below it, which is why every later item measures against a corrected column and depends on this one. Two specific hazards. First, the gutter moving 34 to 32 widens the column by 4px at every width below the cap, so a later item that measured against 34px gutters would read 4px of drift as its own defect — the new numbers are stated here rather than left to be discovered. Second, above a 1440 viewport the page and the design part company unless the cap is expressed the way the design expresses it: the design's 1440 cap CONTAINS its gutters, so its content stops at 1376, while this page's cap is on the content box and would let the column reach 1440. The item has to take a position on that and say which construction it took. This item's gate runs the browser: its oracle command calls measure_page.py --check column-fills-its-page before the floor, so the numbers below are read off a rendered page rather than off the sheet. Two consequences to plan for. The group is this item's to write — the fix and the expectation land in one commit, and an item that changes a value without moving its group fails its own gate. And on a machine with no playwright-cli the harness exits 3 with its skip line, which is not a pass: the item cannot be gated there and must halt for a human rather than merge on a floor that never looked at the page. This item writes its own --check group into skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py, so that file and both its Codex mirrors are declared in touches and the canonical file is declared as a shared resource — which also serializes every group-writing item against the others, so two of them cannot author groups into the same file at once.
contract.preserves: the header's full-bleed, which serve_status.py:1545-1553 documents as deliberate and which the fidelity record books as an intended difference — it is not a finding, and this item does not remove it. Also the hub landing, which shares .wrap but not .wrap--repo and must keep its own narrower measure.
